title: loam chart values
description: Helm validates the COALESCED values (this chart's values.yaml merged with every -f/--set the consumer supplies) against this file before rendering a single template, on `helm template`, `install`, `upgrade` and `lint` alike. Its job here is one specific failure mode, recorded on loam-uwus: without a schema, Helm accepts and silently DISCARDS any key it does not recognise. `--set config.otelEndpoint=... --set terminationGracePeriodSeconds=45` against this chart before those keys existed produced a zero-byte diff against the default render -- a wiring that looked correct, synced green in ArgoCD, exported nothing, and errored nowhere. Every object below therefore DECLARES whether it is closed, which converts an unrecognised key into a render-time failure naming it. Note `declares`, not `closes`: five are deliberately OPEN -- ingress.annotations, nodeSelector, affinity, and both resource shapes -- because each is a verbatim passthrough of a slice of the Kubernetes API (or of arbitrary user-chosen keys) that a partial restatement here would reject valid input for. Each says so in its own description, and internal/deploycheck's TestHelmValuesSchemaExists requires the declaration rather than the answer, so openness is always a recorded decision and never an omission. The cost of the rest is real and accepted: adding a values key means adding it here too, or the chart will not render. That is the trade -- a forgotten schema entry fails loudly on the author's machine, an unvalidated typo fails silently in someone else's cluster.

replicaCount.description: Must be 1. Deliberately NOT bounded above here: templates/_helpers.tpl's loam.validateReplicaCount already fails the render above 1, and schema validation runs BEFORE template execution -- a `maximum: 1` would shadow that helper and replace its full argument (ReadWriteOnce data PVC that a second pod cannot mount, and single-writer ownership of repos.sync_state per sync tick, loam-fp7) with a bare "must be <= 1". The typed check is still worth having, so a string here is caught early.

tag.description: An immutable commit-sha manifest list, never :latest -- see values.yaml.

secret.description: Referenced, never created by this chart. See NOTES.txt for what an operator must provision first.

image.description: Must carry the pgvector extension; loam's migrations create vector columns. Pinned in lockstep with both deploy/docker-compose*.yml, enforced by internal/deploycheck's TestPostgresImageAgrees.

config.description: The non-secret LOAM_* surface, rendered into the loam-config ConfigMap (templates/configmap.yaml). internal/deploycheck asserts this chart can carry every variable internal/config actually reads, and that it names no variable internal/config does not -- both discovered from the Go source, neither written down.

dataDir.description: Must stay in agreement with the volumeMount path in templates/deployment.yaml and the image's own ENV default.

syncInterval.description: A Go duration string. The pattern catches the common shape error -- a bare "60" with no unit, which time.ParseDuration rejects -- and deliberately stops there: it does NOT try to exclude "0s", because expressing "positive" in a regex compiled by Go's RE2 (no lookahead) costs more than it buys when internal/config already rejects a non-positive interval at startup with a legible message.

embedderUrl.description: Absolute http:// or https:// URL of the ollama the embedder talks to. Never deployed by this chart.

embedderModel.description: NOT a free knob: the ingest chunker's byte-per-token bound is specific to nomic-embed-text (loam-c94.16), and vectors already stored were produced by whatever this used to be.

ingestWorkers.description: Bounded above by internal/config's maxIngestWorkers, which exists to catch an operator's typo (an extra zero, a pasted port number) rather than to protect a hard OS limit.

logLevel.description: debug | info | warn | error, matched case-insensitively by internal/config's parseLogLevel. Left as a plain string rather than an enum precisely because of that case-insensitivity: an enum here would reject "INFO", which the server accepts.

otelEndpoint.description: LOAM_OTEL_ENDPOINT, and the ONLY switch that turns telemetry on -- there is deliberately no LOAM_OTEL_ENABLED (internal/config's loadTelemetry). Empty (the default) means no exporter is created at all. The pattern mirrors internal/config's validateOTelEndpoint and catches exactly one mistake: a missing scheme. A bare host:port is worth refusing at render time rather than at container start. THE PORT IS NOT VALIDATED, and http://otel:4317 renders cleanly -- say so rather than implying otherwise, because 4317 is the mistake an operator is most likely to make. loam's exporters speak OTLP over HTTP, whose port is 4318; 4317 is the gRPC port, and a collector listening there accepts the TCP connection and then rejects every payload, which is an unpleasant failure to trace back to a port number. It is left unvalidated because a collector may legitimately be fronted on any port -- refusing 4317 outright would reject a valid reverse-proxied deployment to catch a guess. Example, cross-namespace on the vega cluster: http://otel-gateway.observability.svc.cluster.local:4318

otelServiceName.description: LOAM_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME. Empty (the default) means internal/config's own default, "loam".

otelSampleRatio.description: LOAM_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO, 0..1 inclusive. Empty (the default) means internal/config's own 0.1. Accepts a YAML number or a quoted string, because a valuesObject author writing 0.25 and one writing "0.25" mean the same thing and neither should get a render error. 0 is a legitimate setting and is NOT an off switch -- it silences traces while metrics keep being pushed (docs/server-spec.md); templates/configmap.yaml is written with that in mind.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: DERIVED, not chosen, and the minimum below is the REQUIRED value, not the bare floor. cmd/server/serve.go's defaultShutdownGrace (30s, covering the HTTP drain, the policy-socket close and the background drain, which share one context) plus telemetryFlushGrace (5s, on its own context, strictly after them) gives a 35s floor -- but 35 is exactly the zero margin that made Kubernetes' 30s default wrong in the first place, so requiring it would be requiring the unsafe value. The minimum is floor + 10s of margin for the steps no constant bounds, principally the deferred pgxpool close that runs after the flush; values.yaml shows the arithmetic in full. An earlier version of this file set the minimum to the bare 35 while every other artifact demanded 45, which left the ONE guard a consumer's own valuesObject passes through admitting the value three paragraphs elsewhere call unsafe. This number is not a hand-maintained copy of the Go constants: internal/deploycheck's TestValuesSchemaGracePeriodFloorMatchesGoConstants re-derives floor-plus-margin from cmd/server/serve.go and asserts THIS minimum equals it, so tuning a Go timeout without updating this file is a red test rather than a silently stale bound.

nodeSelector.description: Free-form by nature -- the keys are arbitrary node labels -- so this is open by DECISION, not by omission: values.schema.json closes every other object to unknown keys and internal/deploycheck's TestHelmValuesSchemaExists requires each one to say which it is.

affinity.description: Passed through verbatim to the Pod spec. Open by DECISION: this is a large, deeply nested slice of the Kubernetes API, and a partial restatement of it here would reject valid affinity rules -- a worse failure than accepting an invalid one, which the API server rejects at apply time anyway.

resources.description: A verbatim `toYaml` passthrough into the container's resources block, so this is OPEN by decision -- the same call already made for affinity and nodeSelector above, and it was got wrong here first. An earlier version of this file closed it, which turned `resources.claims` (Dynamic Resource Allocation, Kubernetes 1.26+) into a hard render failure against a chart change that was supposed to be purely additive. requests/limits are named for documentation, not to exclude anything else: a partial restatement of the Kubernetes API rejects valid input, which is worse than accepting input the API server will reject anyway.

resourceQuantities.description: The KEYS here are open, and that is the specific bug this comment exists to prevent recurring: `cpu` and `memory` are merely the common two, and enumerating them made `resources.limits.ephemeral-storage: 1Gi` -- and every extended resource, e.g. `nvidia.com/gpu` -- fail at render against a chart that accepted them the day before. What IS worth constraining is the value SHAPE, since a quantity is always a string or a number and a map or list there is a genuine mistake.
